lesson.title: Causes of Migration in an Interconnected World
lesson.summary: Why millions of people migrated, including free migrants escaping hardship and indentured laborers recruited for plantations.
learningGoals: Explain the causes of migration in the period from 1750 to 1900.
Distinguish free, indentured, and coerced migration.
lesson.bigIdea: Population growth, famine, and industrial demand for labor pushed and pulled tens of millions of people across oceans.
lesson.context: Steamships and railroads made long-distance travel cheaper. The end of slavery in many places created demand for new sources of plantation labor.

sections.title: Push and pull factors

blocks.text: Tens of millions of Europeans emigrated between 1840 and 1914. The Irish famine of 1845 to 1852 killed about a million people and drove more than a million abroad. Others left because farmland was scarce or wages were higher in the Americas.
Many Italians went to Argentina and the United States, and Japanese migrants went to Hawaii and Brazil.

blocks.title: Cause and effect
blocks.text: Famine and land shortage pushed people out, while jobs and wages abroad pulled them, and cheaper steamship travel made the move possible.

sections.takeaway: Push and pull factors combined with new transport to drive mass migration.

sections.title: Indentured labor

blocks.text: After Britain abolished slavery, plantation owners recruited indentured servants. More than a million Indians signed contracts to work, usually for five years, in the Caribbean, Mauritius, Fiji, and southern Africa. Chinese laborers went to Cuba, Peru, and Southeast Asia.

blocks.title: Common trap
blocks.text: Indentured workers were not enslaved, but their contracts limited their freedom and conditions were often harsh.

sections.takeaway: Indenture replaced slavery as a source of plantation labor.

connections.title: From slavery to indenture
connections.body: Unit 4 described the Atlantic slave trade. After abolition, indentured workers from Asia filled many plantation jobs.
connections.transferQuestion: How did abolition affect labor migration?
connections.feedback: Connect the end of slavery to the recruitment of indentured workers.
